description: Cache coherence XSNP_HITM stall misdiagnosed as low cache miss rate
system_prompt: You are a senior systems engineer with deep expertise in Linux internals, distributed systems, networking, and infrastructure operations. Think through the problem carefully — consider all interacting mechanisms before committing to an answer. Show your reasoning chain explicitly before stating conclusions.
user_message:
A single-threaded packet consumer loop on an Intel Raptor Lake CPU (i9-14900K)
reports the following perf stat output:

  518,000,000   instructions      #   0.42 insn per cycle   ← anomalously low
    9,800,000   LLC-load-misses   #   0.38% of all loads    ← low
   14,600,000   branch-misses     #   1.21% of all branches ← low
   18,200,000   dTLB-load-misses  #   0.72% of all loads    ← low
  cpu-clock / task-clock ≈ 1.0                              ← no freq throttling

The loop polls a 1-byte "ready" flag in an mmap-ed ring buffer slot. A producer
thread running on a different physical core writes 1500 bytes of packet data into
the slot, then sets the ready flag. The flag and the packet data share the same
64-byte cache line.

IPC of 0.42 is the only anomalous metric. All standard cache/branch/TLB counters
are low. The obvious diagnosis (LLC miss) does not fit.

(a) Identify the actual bottleneck mechanism. Explain precisely the CPU and cache
    interaction causing the stall, including what state the cache line is in and
    why the LLC-load-miss counter does NOT capture it.
(b) Name the specific perf event or tool that would confirm your diagnosis. Give
    the exact counter name or command.
(c) Propose the minimum-invasive software fix and explain why it works at the
    hardware level.
